holes.name: First Flight
holes.description: A gentle opener. Fairway bunkers pinch the landing area; the green is guarded left and right.

holes.name: The Dogleg
holes.description: Doglegs hard left around a corner bunker. Cut too much off and the trees wait.

holes.name: Pond Hop
holes.description: All carry over the pond to a green that tilts back toward the water.

holes.name: Long Haul
holes.description: The long par five. A creek crosses the fairway just past driving distance: lay up or carry it.

holes.name: Lakeside
holes.description: A lake runs the whole left side and the green leans toward it. Bail out right.

holes.name: Little Sting
holes.description: Short, but the green is ringed by four bunkers. Precision over power.

holes.name: Wingspan
holes.description: A long dogleg right. The inside corner bunker rewards a brave line.

holes.name: Marsh Run
holes.description: A three-shotter past a marsh pond, finishing at a green with water short and right.

holes.name: Home Stretch
holes.description: A cross bunker splits the fairway on the way home to a big, fast green.

holes.name: Ommatidia
holes.description: The compound eye opens the back nine: seven pot bunkers packed in a hexagon, like the facets of a fly's eye, wait just past the drive. Stay left of the cluster.

holes.name: Johnston's Organ
holes.description: The fly's ear: a long par three to a big, tilted green. One long curved bunker sweeps across the front-left like the arista that catches sound; run it in from the right.

holes.name: Halteres
holes.description: Named for the fly's balance organs, which beat opposite the wings: a double dogleg that swings right, then left, with a burn crossing the line of play twice.

holes.name: Protocerebral Bridge
holes.description: A short par four, drivable on paper: a flush driver over a row of church-pew bunkers reaches a small, fast green with water to its right. The pews echo the protocerebral bridge, a row of glomeruli spanning the brain's midline. From the tee the fly is shown the lay-up area on the left, not the pin.

holes.name: Mushroom Body
holes.description: The tee sits in a cup of sand like the calyx; a narrow stalk of fairway, the peduncle, runs out and splits into lobes, one reaching straight up to the green and one turning off to the right.

holes.name: Ellipsoid Body
holes.description: An island green inside a ring of water, the doughnut of neuropil where the fly keeps its compass. A thin causeway at the back right is the only way on foot.

holes.name: Fan-shaped Body
holes.description: The widest hole on the course fans out like the fan-shaped body, crossed by bands of waste sand laid in arcs and broken into columns, as the neuropil is layered and segmented.

holes.name: Giant Fiber
holes.description: The giant fibers are the fly's fastest escape pathway: a pair of huge axons running from the brain straight down to the jump muscles' motor neurons. The longest, straightest hole on the course, a narrow chute through the trees.

holes.name: Descending Neurons
holes.description: Home, the way the brain's commands leave it: down the descending neurons to the body. A cape hole around the clubhouse lake; the more of the water you carry, the shorter the way in.
